fields.title: Purity of Heart
fields.description: Can a heart truly be made pure—free from sin, full of love, and wholly devoted to God? In Purity of Heart, William Booth unfolds the path to inner cleansing, holy living, and spiritual victory. With clarity and urgency, he calls believers to deeper surrender and lasting transformation. Step into this life-changing message—and pursue the purity your soul was made for.

fields.title: Purity: What It Is
fields.body_html:
Matthew 5:8 says, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.”

My Dear Comrades, We Salvationists are always singing or praying or talking about a Pure Heart. Indeed, there are few subjects of which we more frequently speak, or in which we more truly glory. Some of our most beautiful and heart-stirring songs are on this theme. Perhaps, no one is more frequently sung by us than that commencing, "Oh for a heart to praise my God!

A heart from sin set free!

A heart that always feels the Blood, So freely spilt for me! " Isn't that beautiful? But it goes on better still -- "A heart in every thought renewed, And full of Love Divine; Perfect and right, and pure and good, A copy, Lord, of Thine!"

Great, however, as is the power of such songs to stir our hearts, perhaps nothing delights the genuine Salvationist more than the definite testimonies of those living in the enjoyment of the Blessing, or the earnest prayers for its bestowment, or the fervent appeals to Comrades to secure this Pearl of Great Price, so often heard of in our ranks.

And yet many of our Soldiers do not definitely experience and openly profess the enjoyment of the Blessing; and I have been thinking that, perhaps, it is because the subject is not so well understood as it should be. I propose, therefore, to try to explain it in a few Letters, which I hope my Comrades will carefully consider.

Now, please remember that my subject is "Purity of Heart." I want to explain what we mean by a Pure Heart; to show how you may obtain the precious treasure, if you are not possessed of it already; and how you may keep the Blessing when attained. I will start by saying: We all know what is meant by being Pure. When we talk about the purity of things around us, we mean that they are clean and unadulterated. They are not only without dirt or filthiness, but have no inferior substance mixed with them.

When we say that a man is pure, in the religious sense, we mean that he is right and honest and true inside and out; that he not only professes, but practices the things that have to do with his duty to God and man.

Sin is spoken of in the Bible as filthiness or defilement of the body, mind, or spirit. Purity in religion must mean, therefore, the absence of such filthy things as drunkenness, gluttony, dishonesty, cheating, falsehood, pride, malice, bad temper, selfishness, unbelief, disobedience, or the like.

In short, to be pure in soul signifies deliverance from all and everything which the Lord shows you to be opposed to His Holy Will. It means that you not only possess the ability to live the kind of life that He desires, but that you actually do live it.

Now, Purity, I need not tell you, my Comrades, is much admired and greatly desired by all right-minded beings. To begin with: We all like material purity; for instance, I am sure that everyone reading this letter prefers to have a clean body. When you rise in the morning, you are not comfortable till you have washed yourself. When the miners come from the pit, or the farmers from the field, or the girls from the factory, their first demand is for water with which to cleanse themselves.

You like clean clothes and clean linen, right? Consider the money and labor that are expended in keeping your garments clean.You like a clean home. See how the housewife scrubs and washes and brushes and dusts to keep the floor and windows, and furniture clean.

You like a clean city. What a laborious and costly sweeping of the streets, and carrying away of rubbish there is; and what money is spent on the fixing and cleansing of sewers to keep our towns and cities sweet and pure. We like this sort of purity because it is pleasant to the eye and good for health. We know that dirt is hateful to the senses, breeds vermin, generates cholera, plague, and diseases in general, and hurries people to the grave. So, we hate it and say, "Away with it; let us be clean!"

But all right-minded beings admire the purity of the soul far more than they do the purity of the body, or the clothes, the home, or anything else; and that, because it is so much more important.

For instance: (a) God loves Soul Purity. It is His nature to do so. I have no doubt, like us, He prefers to see His children outwardly clean. He tells us, through Apostle Paul, that we are to have our bodies washed with pure water, but the washing of the heart is far more desirable to Him than that of the body.

"His saints are lovely in His sight, He views His children with delight; He sees their hope, He knows their fear, And looks, and loves His image there."

Yes, God delights in Holiness. Heaven, His dwelling place, is pure. Its inhabitants are pure. Its employments, and enjoyments, and worship are all alike pure.

(b) The Angels love Purity. If any unholy creature could, by any means, be introduced into the Celestial City, the inhabitants would, I am sure, avoid such a creature, as we should avoid a being who had some dreadful disease.

(c) The Devils know that Purity is a precious thing, although they hate it and oppose it with all their might.

(d) Many wicked men admire Purity. They look on it as being beautiful and desirable in others, although they regard it as being impossible for them. In their thoughtful moments, when the Spirit of God strives with them, when the recollections of the innocent days gone by crowd into their memories, and they see people who they know are clean and good, they hate themselves because of their own impurity, although all the time refusing to submit to God, and to accept the Salvation that would make them pure.

(e) Lost souls in Hell feel how infinitely superior Holiness is to Wickedness. They now see how much better it would have been for them if they had washed their hearts in the Blood of the Lamb when they had the privilege of doing so. Oh, what would they not give to have such opportunities as those enjoyed by you!

Are you in love with Purity, my friends? Perhaps you possess it. Perhaps you have been to Jesus for the cleansing Power, laid yourselves at His feet, given up your doubtful things, offered yourselves to do His Will, living or dying, and believed that the Blood of Jesus Christ has made you clean.

Oh, if that experience has been yours, happy are you, and happier still if you are walking in the power and peace of that experience today. If it is so, I congratulate you; I delight in you, and praise God on your account.

But if this Blessing is not yours, are you longing after it? Does the thought of it fill your soul with desire? Does it make you feel like the poet, when he sang: "O glorious hope of perfect love!

It lifts me up to things above, It bears on eagles' wings; It gives my ravished soul a taste, And makes me for some moments feast With Jesus' priests and kings."

My friends, your happiness and your influence are all connected with your being made holy. Oh, I beseech you to now kneel here and ask God to make each of you pure, by the Power of the Holy Ghost, through the Blood of the Lamb.

fields.title: Purity Commanded
fields.body_html:
Hebrews 12:14 says, “Follow ... holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.”

My dear friends, Again, I want to take up the subject on which I wrote in my last letter. It is, indeed, a precious topic. I have loved it and talked about it all the way through my religious life; and, today, I regard the enjoyment and publication of the Blessing of a Clean Heart as being as essential to my own peace, power, and usefulness, and as necessary to the progress and prosperity of The Army as ever it was.

A right understanding of the subject will help you to obtain this Blessing for yourselves, and enable you to explain it to others.

In my last letter, I talked about Purity in general; in this, I want to say something on the subject in its practical application to you. What did our dear Lord mean when He spoke of the "Pure in Heart," and pronounced them blessed? What is it to have a Pure Heart? To answer that question, I must begin by asking another: What is meant by the Heart? To which question I answer, we do not mean that organ which you can feel beating in your breast, and which is the central force of the bodily system. That is a very important part of a man, and the keeping of it in good condition is most essential.

But it is not the heart in your body to which Jesus Christ referred in this passage, and about which I want to talk to you, but that power which, being the central force of your soul, may be said to answer to it. As the heart which palpitates in your bosom is the great driving force of the natural man, so the heart we are talking about is the great driving force of the Spiritual Man.

(a) In this sense, it is your Heart that feels joy or sorrow. When you say, "That poor woman died of a broken heart on account of the ill-treatment of her husband," you mean that it was the bitter anguish of her soul which killed her.

(b) It is the Heart that chooses between right and wrong. When you say, "My brother's heart is on the side of God, and goodness, and truth," you mean that these things are the supreme choice of his soul.

(c) It is the Heart that decides on the particular line of conduct to be pursued. When you say, "This young man went to the Mercy-Seat and gave his heart to God," you mean that he decided, in his inmost soul, to accept Salvation and become a Soldier of Christ.

(d) It is the Heart that loves righteousness and hates iniquity. When God says, "My son, give me your heart, He means "Come along, young man or woman, and love Me and holiness, and Souls, and hate the Devil and Sin, with all the powers you possess."

(e) It is the Heart that moulds the character, guides the choice, and masters all the course and conduct of a man's life. The heart is the captain of the ship. It determines whether a man shall accept mercy, serve God, follow righteousness, live for the Salvation of his fellows, and finally enter the Heavenly Harbour in triumph, or whether he shall live a life of rebellion, die in his sins, and finish up a wreck on the rocks of everlasting despair. How important it is to each one of us that we should have a good, right, pure heart.

Now, seeing that the Heart is so thoroughly the master of the man, nothing can be much plainer, can it, my comrades, than the necessity for that Heart being pure? But what is a Pure Heart?

What is it to have a Heart that has been cleansed by the Power of the Holy Spirit through the Blood of Jesus Christ? That is a very important inquiry, and I do hope that my dear soldiers will give me their careful attention while I strive to answer it.

1. And first, a Pure Heart is not a Heart that is never tempted to do evil. Possibly, there is no such thing in this world, nor ever has been, as a Non-Tempted Heart, that is, a man or a woman who has never been exposed to temptation to sin, of one kind or the other. Not only was our Blessed Lord tempted by the Devil in the wilderness, but He was beset with evil attractions all the way through His life. Apostle Paul expressly tells us that our Saviour was in all points tempted like we are, but hallelujah! He resisted the world, the flesh, and the devil, and came through the trying ordeal without a stain. He triumphed over all, for the Apostle exultingly assures us that "He was without sin."

You will be tempted, my comrades, all through your earthly journey, even to the very gates of Heaven; but, thank God, temptation is not sin, and Grace, abundant Grace, is provided to enable you to triumph over all the fascinations of earth and all the devices of hell. You can come off more than a conqueror. But remember, although you may have a Pure Heart, you will have to fight temptation.

2. A Pure Heart is not a Heart that cannot suffer. Beyond question, Jesus Christ had a Pure Heart; He was Holy and undefiled, and yet He was "The Man of Sorrows." Paul tells us that although he exercised himself to have always a conscience void of offence towards God and towards man, yet was he not saved from being, at times, "in heaviness through manifold temptations."

All the Saints of old had hours of darkness and depression, many of them going through seas of anguish. And as with the Saints of old, so is it with the Saints of modern times. It is not sinful to weep and be cast down, if in our distress we do not give way to unbelief and despair and wrongdoing. Cheer up, brothers and sisters! "By floods and flames surrounded," you must "still pursue your way." If you keep believing you will not be confounded, God will deliver you.

3. By a Pure Heart, we do not mean a Heart that cannot sin. The Devil was once a beautiful, sinless creature. But he yielded to temptation. The sinless crown fell from his beautiful brow, and from a pure archangel, he was changed into a foul fiend, and hurled all the way from his bright and sinless Heaven to his dark and gloomy hell. Adam was pure when he came from the hands of his Maker. God pronounced him to be good, but led away by Satan, he lost his Purity, and was cast out of Eden into a world of sin and sorrow and death.

We have the unspeakable sorrow of too frequently seeing Saints and Soldiers fall from Holiness into sin. Some of the many miserable Backsliders around us once walked closely with God, kept their garments unspotted from the world, and were examples of all that is pure and good. But they have gone back to the beggarly elements of the world, and, like the sow that was washed, they are again wallowing in the mire. So, my comrades, you will see that, however pure you may become, it will be possible for you to sin. Though you wash your garments white, and for a season walk with God in holy communion, and have faith so that you can remove mountains and save multitudes, you must remember that while you are in this life, you can fall from Grace.

You must remember that unless you take heed to yourselves, and watch and pray, the probabilities are that you will be overtaken by some besetting sin, and, after having saved others, become yourself a castaway. Therefore, "let him that thinks he stands take heed lest he fall."

4. By a Pure Heart, we do not mean any experience of Purity, however blessed it may be, that cannot increase in enjoyment, usefulness, and power. Pull the weeds out of your garden, and the flowers, plants and trees will grow faster, flourish more abundantly, and become more fruitful.

This very moment, let Jesus Christ purge the garden of your souls of envy and pride, and remove the poisonous plants of malice and selfishness, and every other evil thing, and faith, peace, hope, love, humility, courage, and all the other beautiful flowers of Paradise will flourish in more charming beauty and more abundant fruitfulness.

Oh, will you not go down now before God, and give yourselves fully over into the hands of your precious Saviour? He is waiting to sanctify you. Cast overboard all that hinders. It is God that purifies the Heart. Will you let Him do the work? Now cry out in Faith: "Anger and sloth, desire and pride, This moment be subdued; Be cast into the crimson tide Of my Redeemer's Blood."

But you must go a little further, my Comrades, and, boldly and believingly, sing that song of triumph: 'It is done, this moment save, with full Salvation bless; Redemption through Your Blood I have, and spotless love and peace."

"Come, Holy Ghost, all Sacred Fire, come, fill Your earthly temples now; emptied of every base desire, Reign within, and only You. "Your sovereign right, Your gracious claim, to every thought and every power; our lives to glorify Your name, We yield to You in this sacred hour. "Fill every chamber of the soul; Fill all our thoughts, our passions fill, Till under Your supreme control we submit our cheerful will. 'It is done! Come this moment, my longing soul is all Your own; My heart is Your abiding home. Henceforth, I live for You alone."

fields.title: Purity Means Deliverance
fields.body_html:
Luke 1:74-75 says, “That -- He would grant unto us, that we... might serve Him without fears in holiness and righteousness before Him, all our days.”

My Dear Comrades, I hope I do not tire you by returning once again to the subject of a pure heart. This matter is so important, not only to the Christian Church and the Salvation Army, but to the whole world, that it must be brought forward again.

Holiness has been a great blessing to us in the past, and I am certain it will be an even greater blessing in the future. That is why it must remain at the forefront. You must see its value and clearly understand its meaning.

If you are not living in the peace, power, and joy that holiness brings, it may be because of misunderstandings about it. The devil’s ability to lead people astray in this matter—like in many others—depends greatly on his power to deceive.

So, how can I help you better understand what is meant by purity of heart?

You will remember that in my last letter, I explained what we do not mean. A pure heart does not mean a person cannot be tempted or will never suffer. Nor does it mean that someone who has been cleansed from impurity can no longer sin, or has reached a point beyond growth in faith, hope, love, and the graces of the Holy Spirit.

So then, what is a pure heart?

A pure heart has been cleansed by the Holy Spirit from all sin, and can please God in all it does, to love Him fully, and to love others as oneself. Where this is true, it can rightly be said that God has made that heart pure, just as He is pure.

But some may ask, Doesn’t God do this at conversion? Doesn’t He make a person completely holy the moment He forgives their sins?

My answer is no. Although great work is done at conversion, complete deliverance from sin does not happen all at once. God breaks the power of sin over a person, but the removal of sin from the heart and life is not yet complete.

Let me explain this by describing three states of the soul in relation to sin: 1. Before conversion, sin is the master of the soul. Some desire, habit, or selfish passion controls the person and directs their actions. What does this mean? It means the person is in bondage.

They may see that sin is wrong. They may hate it, struggle against it, and resolve to stop, but they find themselves doing what they do not want to do, and failing to do what they wish to do.

This is the experience of every unconverted person who understands the seriousness of sin. For some, the ruling sin may be obvious, such as drunkenness, lust, dishonesty, or gambling. For others, it may be more hidden, such as pride, ambition, selfishness, or unbelief. But in every case, sin is in control.

2. When a person is saved, they receive not only forgiveness but also freedom from sin’s control.

The chains are broken. The prison doors are opened. They are free. Instead of being ruled by sin, they now have power over it. Instead of being driven toward destruction, they are free to follow God and walk in His will. However, as great as this change is, it is still not complete. While sin no longer rules, its tendencies remain. These inner roots, what Scripture calls “roots of bitterness” continue to cause struggle.

Over time, these inner conflicts may lead to repeated cycles of sin and repentance.

3. Then comes the third stage. Tired of the struggle, grieved by the pride, anger, envy, and selfishness still within, the soul cries out for complete freedom: “Is there no full cure?

Can I never be free from this inward struggle?”

To this cry, God responds with a promise: “I will cleanse you… I will give you a new heart… I will put My Spirit within you…” Then the soul believes. The Holy Spirit comes in power. And this third stage is reached: freedom from all sin.

Examine yourselves. Have you received a pure heart?

Some of you can say with confidence that God has fully sanctified you—that He keeps your whole spirit, soul, and body pure, and will continue to do so. Give Him all the glory. Walk in His light, and remain in fellowship with Him.

But to those who know they do not yet have a pure heart, I ask: Will you receive one now?

God is ready to cleanse you. What is holding you back?

Now is the time. Surrender everything to Him, and come before Him in faith.

fields.title: Purity Described
fields.body_html:
Hebrews 13:20-21 says, “Now may the God of peace who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant, equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.”

My Dear Comrades, Has anything I have said set anyone among you longing after the possession of the precious, the inestimable blessing of a Pure Heart? Has anyone in your Corps been heard singing: "Oh, when shall my soul find her rest, My strugglings and wrestlings be o'er; My heart, by my Saviour possessed, Be fearing and sinning no more?"

It is those who “hunger and thirst for righteousness” who will be filled. If that desire has begun in you, even in a small way, I am glad. Let me help deepen that longing by showing you some of the blessings that come from having a pure heart.

And the first is this: 1. A Pure Heart Produces a Holy Life But what do I mean by a holy life? It is a life that reflects the teachings and promises of Scripture—a life shaped after the example of Jesus Christ. It will not be perfect. There will still be weaknesses and mistakes. But according to the light a person has received, it will be truly holy. Is such a life not worth desiring, my comrades? Is it not a great privilege to live out your faith before your family, your coworkers, and the world? Such a person becomes a blessing wherever they go.

Look at their life: They are honest and faithful in all they do—at work, at home, and in every place. They keep their word. What they promise, they fulfil. They can be trusted, whether seen or unseen. They are diligent. They do not avoid responsibility or waste time, but do their work faithfully. They are kind, loving to their family, gentle with the weak, and compassionate toward those in need. They care deeply for others, seeking the restoration of those who have fallen, and praying for those who are lost. Such a person lives a holy life, not only outwardly, but inwardly. In thought, attitude, and desire, they seek to please God. This is the life that flows from a pure heart. Is this not something to desire? I thank God for those of you who, by His grace, already live in this reality—but I want all of you to enter into it.

2. A Pure Heart Brings Peace A pure heart also brings peace. In fact, true peace cannot exist without it. Now, do not expect a life of constant happiness here on earth—that is not possible. Our human weaknesses, life’s difficulties, and the struggles of living in a broken world make sure of that. But peace—the deep, steady peace of God—is your inheritance. And with a pure heart, it can be yours.

Yes, there will still be battles: You will face opposition from the enemy You will face resistance from the world You will face challenges because you stand for what is right But in a heart that has been cleansed: The struggle with God is over The conflict within the conscience is settled The fear of death and judgment is gone Such a soul has entered into the rest of God.

Do you know this peace, my comrades? Has the inward struggle ended? Do not delay. Let the Holy Spirit, who is ready to make you fully clean, remove everything that stands against your soul. It is not your struggles, your hardships, or your limitations that rob you of peace. Sin is the enemy.

And when pride, laziness, ambition, unbelief, and every other evil is removed, then your peace will flow like a river, and your righteousness will rise like the waves of the sea.

3. A Pure Heart Welcomes the Presence of God Purity of heart is the condition for God to fully dwell within you.

Listen carefully—this is a deep mystery, but it is gloriously true: God desires not only to be with you, but to live in you.

No matter how unnoticed or unimportant you may seem in the eyes of the world, God Himself—the One whom heaven cannot contain—wants to make your heart His home.

Not as a visitor, but as one who stays.

An old writer once said, “God has two homes: one in heaven, and one in the hearts of His people.” God Himself says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with the one who is humble and contrite in spirit…” And again: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock… if anyone opens, I will come in.”

Can you hear Him calling?

Will you not open your heart to Him?

Will you not let go of anything that keeps Him out?

Open the door fully. Welcome Him in—now.

I have much more to say on this precious subject, but it must wait for another time.

Do not delay in seeking full salvation.

fields.title: Purity And Love
fields.body_html:
Romans 6:22 says, “But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life.”

My Dear Comrades, Since writing my last letter, I have been visiting Salvationists in Switzerland, Italy, and France.

Everywhere I go, I see great opportunities for The Salvation Army. Everywhere, I meet dear comrades who long to make the most of these opportunities. And everywhere, it seems to me that what is needed is more red-hot religion to make them equal to the great work before them.

But is it not the same in Great Britain, America, Australia, and every other place where these letters will be read? Is it not the same in your Corps—and even in your own life? As I have explained before, by red-hot religion I mean hearts burning with love for God, for comrades, for those who are lost, for noble work, and for all that is good, both on earth and in heaven. I mean hearts filled with a holy love—a love that compels us to labour and sacrifice for the good of others. A love that makes us servants to those we care about, and gives us power over our own selfish desires. This love reflects the love of our Master: “Not that we loved God, but that He loved us.”

Look at a mother’s love—does it not lead her to give up time, comfort, and even her health for her child? Look at a patriot’s love—does it not lead him to leave behind home and family, and even face death for his country? In the same way, this burning love in a Salvationist will lead them to lay down their time, strength, possessions—everything—at the feet of their Lord, and use it all to bless and save others. It is this spirit of love that creates this holy fire within. Just as the devil stirs up and feeds the fires of pride, selfishness, lust, and other evils—leading people toward destruction—so the intense love produced by the Holy Spirit drives a believer to watch, pray, labour, speak, and even suffer, without concern for the cost, if only they may accomplish the purpose set before them.

But the Holy Spirit dwells in this full power only in hearts that have been cleansed from sin. So, if you truly desire to spend your life blessing others, saving souls, and serving your Lord, you must have a pure heart.

A pure heart will make you a blessing to others—not only because of what you do, but because of who you are. People may be drawn to Christ through your words, your songs, your prayers, and your appeals. But beyond that, if you possess this inner purity, they will also be drawn by what they see in you. Your very life will point them toward God, holiness, and heaven.

As we have seen, a pure heart produces a good life. And goodness is attractive. People are drawn to it and respect it for what it is. Even those who are caught in sin cannot help but admire what is holy. And if this is true for those far from God, how much more will it be true for those who already desire holiness? To such people, your life, if shaped by pure love, will be a constant source of encouragement, strength, and comfort.

This is what we call influence. It is always at work. It is like the fragrance of a rose. Place a flower in a room, and it will quietly fill the space with its scent. You do not need to move it or do anything with it—it simply spreads its fragrance. So it is with the person who has a pure heart and lives in that reality. A holy influence flows from them constantly—not only through what they say and do, but through who they are.

You feel the sincerity and depth of their spirit. When they speak, pray, or reach out to others, something of that inner life comes through. You sense it when you meet them, when you sit with them, or even when you simply look at them. You see it in times of suffering, at the end of life, and even long after they are gone. Years later, even the mention of their name can stir your heart, strengthen your faith, and deepen your love for what is good and true.

Why is this so, my comrades? Because you knew they were holy. You saw their selfless life. You believed they had a pure heart. There is yet another reason to seek a pure heart—it gives you a sure and living hope. This hope is a precious gift. To know that, no matter what troubles come, there is a future filled with peace, joy, and victory—that is something deeply valuable. A person who truly loves God and walks in obedience has a quiet confidence that God will care for them through every trial.

But someone who knows there is still pride, bitterness, or worldliness hidden within, and who neglects their responsibilities, cannot have that same confidence. They may hope for a good future, but it will be uncertain and fragile.

But when a person has both the witness of the Spirit and a consistent life to confirm that inward purity, they can look ahead with confidence, confident of victory, of deliverance, and ultimately of eternal life. Do these things attract you, my comrades? Let me remind you of them. They are truly compelling.

There is the holy life that flows from a pure heart—just as pure water flows from a clean spring.

There is the peace of God, which surpasses understanding. Any remaining sin brings unrest, but purity and peace always go together. There is the presence of God within—a living fire of holy love that purifies motives and transforms the heart. There is a life of usefulness and influence that continues to speak long after you are gone. And there is the bright hope of eternity—the promise of glory and reward to come.

All of this, my comrades, depends on one thing: a pure heart. These are only some of the countless blessings that flow from this source of purity and power. Do you have this treasure? If you do, give thanks to God. If you do not, seek it now.

fields.title: Purity Possible
fields.body_html:
Hebrews 13:12 says, “So Jesus also suffered outside the gate in order to sanctify the people through his own blood.”

My Dear Comrades, I can easily imagine that some of my Soldiers, after reading what I have written about a pure heart, may be asking, “Is it really possible for me to receive this?” I know that many people outside our ranks openly say that such an experience is impossible. They claim that no one can live in this world without sinning. They argue that no matter how much we hate sin, grieve over it, pray against it, or trust in Christ for victory, we must continue in defeat—sinning and repenting again and again until the end of life.

In response to this, I stand with the Apostle John and affirm that God is not only willing and able to forgive sin, which no believer in Scripture would deny, but that He is equally willing and able to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. But before we go further, let us be clear about what is being said. I am declaring nothing less than this: that God can keep you from sin.

Some may ask, “What is sin?” The Apostle John answers this plainly: “All unrighteousness is sin.” In other words, anything we do—or allow—in thought, desire, or action, which we know to be wrong, is sin. Now I affirm, on the authority of Scripture, that Jesus Christ your Saviour is both willing and able to keep you from doing what is wrong. He was called Jesus because He would “save His people from their sins.”

As I have said before, you may still face temptation. You may experience discouragement, physical pain, confusion of mind, or deep sorrow. The world may oppose you. Dark seasons may come. You may even feel, as Christ did on the cross, abandoned. Yet, in the midst of all this, you can still be kept from sin. In the name of the Lord, I declare that it is possible for you to have and to keep a pure heart. Many of you already believe this. But for those who still struggle with doubt, let me make it clearer.

First, you cannot doubt God’s ability to do this. He created you, sustains you, redeemed you, forgave you, and has promised you eternal life. Surely, then, He is able to keep you from sin during the short time you remain on earth. I am certain that He can.

Yes, it may seem difficult. Your circumstances may be challenging. There may be pressures in your home or work that oppose a holy life. You may have tried before and failed. You may feel overwhelmed with doubt or even despair. But God is greater than all of this. He has already delivered you from many sins. Habits and desires that once controlled you have been broken.

Some have even been completely removed. Why, then, should He not complete the work?

“Finish, then, Your new creation, Pure and spotless, let me be; Let me see Your great salvation, Perfectly restored in You.”

There is no reason to doubt His power. He keeps the angels from falling; they do not keep themselves. It is His strength that sustains them. He will keep you from sin in heaven, and He is able to keep you now. You already believe that He is mighty to save. You have sung it again and again: “All things are possible to him That can in Jesus’ name believe…” And if God is able to make and keep you pure, you cannot doubt His willingness to do so. This is just as clear. In fact, it is something you must not only understand, but feel deeply, that Jesus Christ is not only able, but ready and waiting, even now, to remove from your heart the very things that have troubled and burdened you for so long. The very nature of God proves His willingness. All beings act according to their nature. Wicked people are drawn to evil. Good people delight in what is good. God is holy. He declares it again and again. And because He is holy, He must hate sin and delight in making people holy like Himself.

Nothing would please Him more than to remove everything unclean from your life. Will you let Him? God also clearly tells us in Scripture that this is His desire: “Put on the new self… created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.”

“Be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect.”

“This is the will of God, your sanctification.”

Jesus Christ came into the world, lived, suffered, died, and rose again for this very purpose, that you might be made holy. Scripture tells us that He came to destroy the works of the devil, and to cleanse and prepare His people so that they may be holy and without fault. His love for you also proves His willingness. No human love, whether for wealth, country, family, or anything else, can compare to the love God has for you. And because He knows that sin is your greatest enemy, He longs to deliver you from it.

God has also promised you a clean heart if you seek Him. He calls you to separate yourself from sin, and He promises to receive you as His own. And we know He is willing because He has already done this for so many others—both in the past and in our present time. He shows no favouritism. What He has done for others, He will do for you. You are just as welcome to be made clean.

“Will you now enter in?

Will you wash and be clean?”

fields.title: Purity, God's Gift
fields.body_html:
2 Corinthians 4:7 says, “But we have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us.”

My Dear Comrades, I now come to one of the most important parts of this subject: How can a Pure Heart be obtained? I can almost hear the question rising within you: “It is good, precious, and desirable—but how can I have it?”

Let us take a brief look back at the ground we have covered together.

First, we considered what holiness truly is—not a constant emotional high, nor a life that allows room for sin. Then we saw its value: peace, usefulness, and the continued favour of God. We also established that this life is possible for anyone—young or old, rich or poor—because God is able to cleanse and sustain a holy life.

Now we come to the heart of the matter: How is it obtained? Two Powers at Work. When you ask, “What must I do to be pure?” the answer is this: something must be done, and part of it rests with you.

There are two forces involved: The Divine — God The Human — You God and man work together, just as in everyday life. You labour, and God provides. At conversion, you repented and believed—and God saved you. It is the same here. From beginning to end, it is God who saves. Fix that truth firmly in your mind: a Pure Heart comes from God alone. Only He can remove pride, anger, selfishness, and every inward sin—and replace them with love and peace. This is the work of the Holy Spirit, the cleansing fire. What a comfort—to know that the One who is able is also willing.

Your Part: Faith While God does the work, your responsibility is clear: you must believe. Scripture teaches that the heart is purified by faith. When a soul comes to God, yields fully to His will, and trusts Him to cleanse it—that very moment, the work is done. Faith says, “It is mine now.”

What Will Not Cleanse the Heart Let us be clear about what cannot produce this purity: 1. Not human effort No person can cleanse your heart—not a preacher, not a leader, not a friend. Only Christ can do that.

2. Not religious activity alone Meetings, prayers, and songs help, but without true faith, they are empty.

3. Not knowledge You may understand holiness deeply and still never experience it.

4. Not repentance alone Many feel sorrow for sin and try to change, but stop short of believing in full deliverance.

5. Not consecration alone You may offer yourself to God, but without His power, you cannot live it out.

The Final Step All these may lead you forward—but there is one step you must take: Faith.

You may say: “I desire” “I repent” “I surrender” But will you say: “I believe God cleanses me now.”

That is the final step—the moment where desire becomes reality.

fields.title: Purifying Faith
fields.body_html:
Ephesians 3:17-19 says, “So that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may have strength to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.”

My Dear Comrades, You will remember that when I closed my last letter, I was speaking about a very important part of our subject—namely, that act of faith which purifies the heart. I said something then, but I must return to it, because it is here that many stumble and fail in seeking the blessing of purity.

They come right up to the door of full deliverance from sin. They look inside the temple of holiness. They long to enter. And yet, they hesitate to take the one step that would carry them in.

They do not exercise the faith that purifies. And so they turn back—returning to that unsatisfying life of sinning and repenting in which they have remained for so long.

I am convinced this often comes from misunderstanding. And so, I want to make this matter clearer—what that faith really is by which the soul enters into full salvation. I may repeat some things we have already considered. But that is better than leaving you uncertain. I would rather say it a hundred times and be understood.

Purifying faith begins with some clear understanding of the blessing itself. That understanding may not be perfect, but it must be enough to grasp what purity really means. It is not a passing feeling. It is not merely relief from temptation. It is not constant emotional excitement. It is a state of heart in which a person no longer grieves the Spirit of God, but loves Him fully and obeys Him sincerely. This kind of faith fixes its attention on the blessing and says, “I want a pure heart. I need it. It is God’s will for me. Christ purchased it for me. Lord, let it be mine.”

Has your faith reached that point? Do you truly see what purity is? If so, hold on to that understanding until the blessing becomes yours. When a person truly sees something valuable and possible, desire begins to grow. The more you think about it, the more you consider it, the more it draws you. So it is with holiness. If you believe it is as precious as it truly is, you will keep it before your mind, and your desire for it will deepen.

But purifying faith does not stop at desire. It goes further. It chooses. It does not merely admire or speak or wish. It says, “I will have it.” We see how people treat salvation itself—they acknowledge its value, yet delay seeking it. And in the same way, many treat holiness. They say, “I should be holy. I wish I were holy. Lord, make me holy—but not now.”

But real faith does not delay. It chooses, and it begins at once. This faith also gives up whatever stands in the way. When something is truly valued, people are willing to let go of lesser things to obtain it. So it is here. If you truly believe in the worth of purity, you will be ready to part with anything that hinders you. It will not argue. It will not hold back. It will surrender.

And this brings us to a point where many hesitate. They shrink from full surrender. They fear what God may require of them. They wonder where He may send them, or what He may ask them to do. And so they draw back—and go no further. But purifying faith sees Christ differently. It sees Him as altogether worthy. It sees His service as good. And so it lays everything down willingly, without condition, without reserve, ready to be used in any way He chooses. Such a surrender has no limits, except the limits of one’s ability. This faith also rests on what God has already done. It understands that holiness has been purchased by Christ and promised in His Word. It hears God say, “I will cleanse you,” and it responds, “Yes, Lord—I believe it shall be so.”

But it goes even further than that. It does not only believe that God is willing. It believes that God is doing it now. And so I ask you—when will this purity come to you? Will you say tomorrow? Perhaps—but who can be sure? Will you say at the hour of death? Perhaps—but who can promise that? Why not now? For now is the accepted time. Now is the day of salvation.

fields.title: Witnesses
fields.body_html:
Acts 1:8 says, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

My Dear Comrades, Have you grown tired of this subject? I trust not. For myself, from my earliest days until now, the subject of holiness has never lost its beauty. To speak of the power of Christ to cleanse the heart, to fill it with love, and to keep it from falling, has always been one of the greatest joys of my life.

And it remains so still.

Surely, we ought to make this known—not only with our words, but with our lives—that Jesus Christ came not only to forgive sin, but to cleanse the heart and make it pure. But perhaps some of you still doubt. You may wonder whether such a life is truly possible. Let us then hear the testimony of others. We begin with those whose lives are recorded in Scripture. Enoch walked with God for three hundred years and pleased Him. Noah was called righteous in his generation.

Job was declared upright, a man who trusted God even in suffering. Abraham obeyed God fully, even when the cost was great. Isaiah was cleansed and immediately yielded himself to God’s service. Zacharias and Elizabeth were described as righteous, walking blamelessly before God.

John spoke of perfect love. Paul could appeal to others as witnesses to the holiness of his life.

These are not small testimonies. They show what God is able to do. And if we look beyond Scripture, we find the same witness repeated. John Fletcher declared that he was dead to sin and that Christ was his all in all. Others have spoken of a moment when God’s power came upon them—not in judgment, but in love—filling them with a new life. Another testified that he had walked in this liberty for many years, kept by the power of God. These are not imaginations.

They are real experiences. And so, my comrades, you are left with a decision. You have heard that such a life is possible. You have seen that God is able and faithful. You have been shown the way.

What will you do?

Your Lord is waiting to bring you into this life of purity and love.

Do not delay.

Enter in—by faith.

And if at first you do not succeed, do not give up. Continue. Seek again. Trust again. For the promise remains sure.

fields.title: How To Keep Pure
fields.body_html:
James 1:12 says, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him.”

My Dear Comrades, After trying to show you the desirability of this experience, and urging it upon your acceptance, I cannot help feeling that a few counsels bearing upon the best method of retaining the blessing of Holiness after it has been gained may be useful. Beyond question, many do find this sacred treasure of a Pure Heart, and exult in the confidence and joy it brings, who, after a short season, lose it again. They enter the Holy Temple, and then, for one reason or another, desert it. They struggle with tears and prayers up onto the Highway of Holiness, and then turn aside onto some by path or other, where they become the prey once more of the doubts and fears and sins of the olden time. This is a great pity.

Those who act thus are the chief sufferers; but, alas! A great injury is also inflicted upon others by their unfaithfulness. But the failure of those who obtain the grace to keep what they have received should be no discouragement to you who have entered upon this holy path, and no argument against your persevering in it.

What you have to do, my Comrades, is to make up your minds that having found the Pearl of Great Price, no enemy shall rob you of the treasure. To this end, my first counsel is: 1. Seek till you obtain a settled conviction in your own heart that the work is done. Be content with nothing less than the assurance that God has really and truly cleansed your soul from sin.

Do not allow yourselves to rest in any pleasant feelings merely, or in any hope of a future revelation on the subject. Continue to wrestle, and pray, and believe, until you are satisfied that the work is accomplished.

But do you ask again, "How can I tell whether God has cleansed my soul from sin?" I reply, "How did you find out that God had forgiven your sins? How did you come to know that precious fact? For assuredly, a precious fact it was when you were saved. I suppose that since that gracious gift was yours, you have sung over a thousand times or more, the words:" "I never shall forget the day When Jesus washed my sins away."

"How did you come to the personal assurance that you were saved?" I ask, and you reply that God spoke it to your heart. Well, the assurance of your Sanctification will come in the same way.

The Holy Spirit will produce a delightful persuasion in your soul that all the pride and malice, and envy and selfishness, have been taken away, and that God has filled you with peace and love.

This precious persuasion will, no doubt, come in different forms to different individuals. To some it will appear as the "Rest of Faith," to others as the "Baptism of Fire," to others as the "Fullness of Love," and to others as the Enthronement of Christ come to reign in their souls supreme over an inward Kingdom, which is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

But to all alike, when the work is real and complete, there will be the conviction that the blood cleanses and that the heart is pure. Be content with nothing less than this, and leave to God's good pleasure the giving or the withholding of more.

2. Being satisfied that God has purified your heart, confess the fact. You must do so if you want to retain the Blessing. Many of the Holiest men and women the world has known have, under the influence of false modesty or diffidence or other motives, been hindered from avowing the wonderful things that God has done for them, and have thereby grieved the Holy Spirit and lost the Blessing. Satan will tempt you to hide your light under a bushel after the same manner, but you must resist him and boldly confess to all around you the Salvation God has given you.

Acknowledge it to yourselves. Say over and over again to your own heart: "Glory, Glory, Jesus saves me; Glory, Glory to the Lamb"; Now the Cleansing Blood has reached me, Glory, Glory to the Lamb!"

Acknowledge it to your Saviour. Tell Him that you trust Him, and glorify Him for what He has done for you. Confess it to your Comrades at every reasonable opportunity. Let it be known in your own family. It may not only greatly help you, for those nearest and dearest to you to know what God has done for you, but it may prove a great blessing to them. Of course, you will be careful not to exhibit anything like a boastful spirit, and to give all the glory to God for all that He has given you to enjoy, and I am sure you will not make any professions as though you condemned those Comrades who have not been brought to see and possess this great Salvation. Love will be in all your words as well as in your heart.

But you must confess the fact that God has cleansed your heart, and that, by His Spirit, He enables you to live day by day without grieving Him. It may be, at times, it will be a cross. But you must take it up, and in doing so, you will become a light and a power and a joy to your Comrades and friends.

3. To retain the Blessing, you must strive to live in the same spirit of submission, obedience, and consecration to God as that which you entered into its enjoyment. Your everyday experience must be that which we often sing: "Here then to You your own I leave, Mould as You will Your passive clay, But let me receive Your stamp And let me all Your words obey, Serve with a single heart and eye, And to Your glory live and die."

4. To keep this experience, you must continue in the same spirit of trust that first brought the Blessing into your heart. You did not receive the gift of Purity by feelings or by knowledge or by works; no, nor by desire nor by prayer. You believed, and you were saved. If you had said I won't, or I can't believe that Jesus cleanses, unless I feel the work to be done in my heart, you could not have rejoiced in its possession. You trusted, and the work was done. You must go forward in that spirit. There will be hours when all will seem to be hard and dark and desolate.

Those will be hours when you will have to fight the fight of faith, and to cling to the beginning of your confidence, whether you feel pleasant or unpleasant, whether your heart seems hard or tender, that the Blood cleanses. Hold it fast.

5. To keep a clean heart, you must resist temptation. You will have temptation, it will come from different sources, but especially from the devil, in three particular directions: -- (a) He will try to draw you aside into old habits, either doubtful in their nature or positively evil.

He will know your weak points. Set a double watch there.

(b) He will suggest his own evil wishes and desires, and then seek to persuade you that they are from your own heart. He will say, "How can you be sanctified and have such sinful thoughts as those?" Disown his foul productions. Tell him they are not yours. Tell him that you hate them.

Tell him they belong to him.

(c) He will strive to make you think you have lost the Blessing because you do not always feel as though you have it. But you are to live not by feeling but by faith.

6. To keep a pure heart, you must carefully continue the use of such means as God has appointed for your assistance. Purity does not bring you into any state that renders the use of means for its maintenance and increase unnecessary.

7. To keep the Blessing: (a) You must pray, and I strongly urge you to pray at stated hours and for given periods.

(b) You must read and study your Bible.

(c) Read such books and papers as are instructive and encouraging on the subject of Holiness.

(d) Watch as well as pray. Be ever on your guard.

8. Keep on fighting for souls, do not be led off into a selfish occupation with your own experience, or in promoting the same experience in other Comrades. I think it is proper that you should devote a portion of your time and energy to the duty of sanctifying yourselves and of spreading a full Salvation among your Comrades. But nothing can relieve you from the duty of fighting for the Salvation of dying souls around you.

I have only space for one other word. It is of deep importance. With all the emphasis I can command I would say to every reader of these Letters, if from any cause whatever you should lose the assurance that the blood of Jesus cleanses you; or if, more melancholy still, you should lose the blessing of Purity, fly at once to your Saviour's feet, confess your wrongdoing, give yourself up again to the full service of your Lord, and once more plunge in the Fountain opened for sin and uncleanness; and then, profiting by the sorrow and disappointment of your fall, start afresh to live the life of faith in a purifying Saviour.

"What though a thousand hosts engage A thousand worlds my soul to shake, I have a shield that shall quell their rage, And drive the alien armies back: Portrayed it bears a bleeding Lamb, I dare believe in Jesus' name.

"Me to retrieve from Satan's hands, Me from this evil world to free, To purge my sins and lose my bands, And save from all iniquity, My Lord and God from heaven He came; I dare believe in Jesus' name."

--- THE END ---
fields.body_text: James 1:12 says, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him.” My Dear Comrades, After trying to show you the desirability of this experience, and urging it upon your acceptance, I cannot help feeling that a few counsels bearing upon the best method of retaining the blessing of Holiness after it has been gained may be useful. Beyond question, many do find this sacred treasure of a Pure Heart, and exult in the confidence and joy it brings, who, after a short season, lose it again. They enter the Holy Temple, and then, for one reason or another, desert it. They struggle with tears and prayers up onto the Highway of Holiness, and then turn aside onto some by path or other, where they become the prey once more of the doubts and fears and sins of the olden time. This is a great pity. Those who act thus are the chief sufferers; but, alas! A great injury is also inflicted upon others by their unfaithfulness. But the failure of those who obtain the grace to keep what they have received should be no discouragement to you who have entered upon this holy path, and no argument against your persevering in it. What you have to do, my Comrades, is to make up your minds that having found the Pearl of Great Price, no enemy shall rob you of the treasure. To this end, my first counsel is: 1. Seek till you obtain a settled conviction in your own heart that the work is done. Be content with nothing less than the assurance that God has really and truly cleansed your soul from sin. Do not allow yourselves to rest in any pleasant feelings merely, or in any hope of a future revelation on the subject. Continue to wrestle, and pray, and believe, until you are satisfied that the work is accomplished. But do you ask again, "How can I tell whether God has cleansed my soul from sin?" I reply, "How did you find out that God had forgiven your sins? How did you come to know that precious fact? For assuredly, a precious fact it was when you were saved. I suppose that since that gracious gift was yours, you have sung over a thousand times or more, the words:" "I never shall forget the day When Jesus washed my sins away." "How did you come to the personal assurance that you were saved?" I ask, and you reply that God spoke it to your heart. Well, the assurance of your Sanctification will come in the same way. The Holy Spirit will produce a delightful persuasion in your soul that all the pride and malice, and envy and selfishness, have been taken away, and that God has filled you with peace and love. This precious persuasion will, no doubt, come in different forms to different individuals. To some it will appear as the "Rest of Faith," to others as the "Baptism of Fire," to others as the "Fullness of Love," and to others as the Enthronement of Christ come to reign in their souls supreme over an inward Kingdom, which is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost. But to all alike, when the work is real and complete, there will be the conviction that the blood cleanses and that the heart is pure. Be content with nothing less than this, and leave to God's good pleasure the giving or the withholding of more. 2. Being satisfied that God has purified your heart, confess the fact. You must do so if you want to retain the Blessing. Many of the Holiest men and women the world has known have, under the influence of false modesty or diffidence or other motives, been hindered from avowing the wonderful things that God has done for them, and have thereby grieved the Holy Spirit and lost the Blessing. Satan will tempt you to hide your light under a bushel after the same manner, but you must resist him and boldly confess to all around you the Salvation God has given you. Acknowledge it to yourselves. Say over and over again to your own heart: "Glory, Glory, Jesus saves me; Glory, Glory to the Lamb"; Now the Cleansing Blood has reached me, Glory, Glory to the Lamb!" Acknowledge it to your Saviour. Tell Him that you trust Him, and glorify Him for what He has done for you. Confess it to your Comrades at every reasonable opportunity. Let it be known in your own family. It may not only greatly help you, for those nearest and dearest to you to know what God has done for you, but it may prove a great blessing to them. Of course, you will be careful not to exhibit anything like a boastful spirit, and to give all the glory to God for all that He has given you to enjoy, and I am sure you will not make any professions as though you condemned those Comrades who have not been brought to see and possess this great Salvation. Love will be in all your words as well as in your heart. But you must confess the fact that God has cleansed your heart, and that, by His Spirit, He enables you to live day by day without grieving Him. It may be, at times, it will be a cross. But you must take it up, and in doing so, you will become a light and a power and a joy to your Comrades and friends. 3. To retain the Blessing, you must strive to live in the same spirit of submission, obedience, and consecration to God as that which you entered into its enjoyment. Your everyday experience must be that which we often sing: "Here then to You your own I leave, Mould as You will Your passive clay, But let me receive Your stamp And let me all Your words obey, Serve with a single heart and eye, And to Your glory live and die." 4. To keep this experience, you must continue in the same spirit of trust that first brought the Blessing into your heart. You did not receive the gift of Purity by feelings or by knowledge or by works; no, nor by desire nor by prayer. You believed, and you were saved. If you had said I won't, or I can't believe that Jesus cleanses, unless I feel the work to be done in my heart, you could not have rejoiced in its possession. You trusted, and the work was done. You must go forward in that spirit. There will be hours when all will seem to be hard and dark and desolate. Those will be hours when you will have to fight the fight of faith, and to cling to the beginning of your confidence, whether you feel pleasant or unpleasant, whether your heart seems hard or tender, that the Blood cleanses. Hold it fast. 5. To keep a clean heart, you must resist temptation. You will have temptation, it will come from different sources, but especially from the devil, in three particular directions: -- (a) He will try to draw you aside into old habits, either doubtful in their nature or positively evil. He will know your weak points. Set a double watch there. (b) He will suggest his own evil wishes and desires, and then seek to persuade you that they are from your own heart. He will say, "How can you be sanctified and have such sinful thoughts as those?" Disown his foul productions. Tell him they are not yours. Tell him that you hate them. Tell him they belong to him. (c) He will strive to make you think you have lost the Blessing because you do not always feel as though you have it. But you are to live not by feeling but by faith. 6. To keep a pure heart, you must carefully continue the use of such means as God has appointed for your assistance. Purity does not bring you into any state that renders the use of means for its maintenance and increase unnecessary. 7. To keep the Blessing: (a) You must pray, and I strongly urge you to pray at stated hours and for given periods. (b) You must read and study your Bible. (c) Read such books and papers as are instructive and encouraging on the subject of Holiness. (d) Watch as well as pray. Be ever on your guard. 8. Keep on fighting for souls, do not be led off into a selfish occupation with your own experience, or in promoting the same experience in other Comrades. I think it is proper that you should devote a portion of your time and energy to the duty of sanctifying yourselves and of spreading a full Salvation among your Comrades.
